topics.label: Course introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series, its multidisciplinary audience, and the key learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Biological and experimental definitions of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore cancer as a multi-step breakdown of normal developmental differentiation and tissue architecture, alongside the experimental models used to study tumor cells.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and benign versus malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how tumors progress from contained benign lesions to invasive and metastatic malignancies, using histological features and tissue models to illustrate the transition.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard conventions and exceptions used to name and classify tumors according to their tissue of origin and malignancy.

topics.label: Pathophysiological causes of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the local, systemic, and metastatic mechanisms through which tumors impair normal physiological function and cause patient death.

topics.label: Patterns of cancer incidence across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze the comparative frequency and tissue distribution of tumors in human populations and across diverse multicellular animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and applications of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the clinical necessity, methodology, and varying efficacy of population screening programs for detecting pre-malignant and early-stage cancers.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a reminder of the learning outcomes and logistical framing for upcoming practical sessions.
